question: Why do worn jeans fade towards white instead of a paler, even blue?
answer: Because the dye never reached the middle of the thread. Indigo is built up in repeated dips and clings to the outside of the cotton yarn, leaving a white core, and only the lengthwise warp threads are dyed; the crosswise weft stays undyed. Rubbing at knees and pockets strips the blue skin off each thread.
move: How a thing wears out tells you how it was built.
reference: James Sullivan, Jeans: A Cultural History of an American Icon, Gotham Books, 2006
